shape: A, không phải B. Or two sentences where the second one negates the first. A comma-joined negation is not counted here - `Bốn món trên bảng, không có món phụ` is a second fact rather than a contrast, and the sentence-final version is caught by clipped-parallel anyway
pattern: (?i)(?:[.;!?]\s*|\s—\s)(?:không|never\b|not\b)|\b(không phải|chứ không|nhưng không|thay vì|rather than|instead of)\b
why_it_reads_machine: The strongest device available for stating a principle, which is why a model reaches for it every time it has a principle to state. One is a position. Four on one page is a tic, and the reader stops hearing the position and starts hearing the machine
fix: Keep the one where the negation is the news - where a reader genuinely expected B. Rewrite the others as the positive half only, and let the contrast be implied by what you did not say

shape: X đi vào. Y đi ra.
pattern: (?i)\b(đi vào|đưa vào|goes in|in)\b[^\n]{0,45}\b(đi ra|đưa ra|comes out|out)\b
why_it_reads_machine: A pipeline description wearing a headline. It tells the reader what the machine does to an input, which is a fact about the maker's process and not about the reader's situation
fix: Name what the reader walks away holding. The transformation is the mechanism, and the mechanism belongs one line below the title

shape: Two or more sentences in one title, each five words or fewer
why_it_reads_machine: Full stops used as a rhythm instrument. It reads as deliberate the first time and as a template by the third, and it is the single most recognisable shape in machine-written headline copy
fix: One sentence. If two facts genuinely both belong in the title, the title is doing the job of a title and a deck, so split it into a title and a deck

shape: Title: the part that explains the title
why_it_reads_machine: The colon lets a writer avoid choosing. Everything before it is a gesture and everything after it is the actual sentence, so the reader pays for the first half twice
fix: Delete the left half and check whether anything was lost. Usually the right half was the headline

shape: Bí mật / điều ít ai biết / sự thật đằng sau
pattern: (?i)\b(bí mật|bí quyết|bật mí|hé lộ|sự thật đằng sau|điều ít ai biết|điều không ai nói|ít ai biết|bạn sẽ không tin)\b
why_it_reads_machine: It withholds the only thing the title had to give. There is no version of this that is not a promise to pay the reader later, and the reader has been paid later before
fix: State the fact. If the fact is not interesting enough to be the headline, the problem is upstream of the headline

shape: The secret to / what nobody tells you / you won't believe
pattern: (?i)\b(the secret (to|of)|what nobody tells you|you won'?t believe|this one trick|here'?s why you)\b
why_it_reads_machine: Same withholding, and in English it additionally dates the copy to a decade of content marketing the reader has learned to scroll past
fix: State the fact, and put the number in it if there is one

shape: Khám phá / đừng bỏ lỡ / nhanh tay
pattern: (?i)^(khám phá|tìm hiểu ngay|đừng bỏ lỡ|nhanh tay|chốt ngay|mua ngay|xem ngay|trải nghiệm ngay)\b
why_it_reads_machine: An order given to a stranger who has not agreed to be addressed. In Vietnamese it is doubly wrong because the imperative with no addressee and no particle reads as signage rather than speech
fix: Replace the verb with the thing. A noun the reader recognises does the work the imperative was trying to force

shape: Unlocking / Elevating / Mastering / Transforming
why_it_reads_machine: The most heavily fingerprinted opening in machine-written English. It also has no subject, so nobody is doing the unlocking and nothing is being unlocked in particular
fix: Name the actor and the object. If neither is nameable, there is no title here yet

shape: Tất tần tật về / hướng dẫn A-Z / the ultimate guide to
pattern: (?i)(tất tần tật|từ a ?- ?z|từ a đến z|hướng dẫn (toàn diện|chi tiết|đầy đủ)|the (ultimate|complete|definitive) guide|everything you need to know)
why_it_reads_machine: A claim about the document's own completeness, made by the document. It is unfalsifiable and it is always the first thing to be untrue
fix: Title the piece with the one thing it settles. Completeness is the reader's verdict to reach, not the title's claim to make

shape: Top 5 / 7 điều / 10 ways
why_it_reads_machine: The number is about how the writer organised the work. A reader who wanted five of something would already know they wanted five
fix: Lead with the most useful item on the list. If none of them can carry a headline alone, the list is padding

shape: Any X nhất, or hàng đầu / premium / best, with no figure anywhere in the title. Ordinals (thứ nhất) and uniqueness (duy nhất) are excluded - neither is a comparison
why_it_reads_machine: A superlative is a comparison, and a comparison with no measurement is the shape of a claim without the claim. It is also the exact wording an advertising regulator asks you to substantiate
fix: Either put the measurement in the title or delete the superlative. `Nhanh nhất` with no number is weaker than a stated number with no superlative

shape: Câu — rồi phần hé lộ
why_it_reads_machine: Vietnamese punctuates this with a comma, a colon or a full stop. The em dash arrives with the English draft, and in a title there is no sentence long enough to have earned it
fix: Comma, colon or full stop. The pause you wanted is available in all three

shape: Statement — the reveal
why_it_reads_machine: The em dash is the default rhythmic tool with nothing pushing back on it, so it repeats. One per set of titles is a choice; two is a habit
fix: Keep the one where the dash carries a genuine reversal. Elsewhere use a comma

shape: brief / output / pipeline / hệ thống / cơ chế / bố cục as the subject
why_it_reads_machine: This is the defect underneath most of the others. The title is written last, by the person who just built the thing, so the freshest noun in their head is the one from the workshop - and the reader has never been in the workshop
fix: Swap the workshop noun for the reader's noun: the thing they hold, sell, lose or wait for. Keep the workshop noun only where the reader's job is literally to buy the system

shape: Việc tối ưu hoá quy trình / Sự thay đổi của thị trường / Quá trình sản xuất nội dung
why_it_reads_machine: An English noun phrase pushed through Vietnamese. It is grammatical and nobody speaks it, which is the exact signature of a translated draft
fix: Start on the verb or the object. Vietnamese drops the subject natively and does not need the abstract noun to hold the front of the sentence

shape: Bạn có muốn…? / Are you tired of…?
pattern: (?i)^(bạn có (muốn|biết|đang)|bạn đã bao giờ|do you want|have you ever|are you (tired|looking|struggling))\b
why_it_reads_machine: A question everybody answers yes to filters nobody, so it is a statement wearing a question mark. `copy-formulas.csv` already says this under question-open; a title is where it happens most
fix: Ask something only your actual buyer would say yes to, or state the thing instead

shape: !! / ?! / a title ending in an exclamation mark
why_it_reads_machine: Volume substituting for the news. The exclamation mark asks the reader to supply the excitement the sentence did not
fix: Delete it. If the sentence needs it to land, rewrite the sentence

shape: 2026 mới nhất / latest 2026
why_it_reads_machine: Written for a ranking algorithm rather than a person, and it expires on a fixed date whether or not the content did
fix: Date the fact, not the title. `Giá tháng 8` is a fact; `mới nhất 2026` is a maintenance liability

shape: Three comma-separated items in one title
why_it_reads_machine: Three is the length a list defaults to when nobody counted. `slop-tells.csv` carries this for body copy; in a title it costs more because there is no room to make any of the three specific
fix: Pick the one that decides the reader. Two of the three were there for rhythm

shape: và / and / cùng với inside the title
why_it_reads_machine: `copy-formulas.csv` one-idea-headline states the rule: there is no situation where two ideas in one headline is correct. The conjunction is where the second idea gets in
fix: Cut to the idea that would survive alone. The other one is a subhead or it is nothing

shape: A figurative noun the page never introduces - dấu vân tay, hành trình, DNA
why_it_reads_machine: A metaphor is a loan against context the reader has not been given yet. In body copy the next paragraph repays it; a title has no next paragraph, so it stays a debt
fix: Use the literal noun in the title and put the metaphor in the body where it can be paid for. If the metaphor is the only interesting thing, the literal fact was too weak to ship
